problem: Waypoint predictors in continuous VLN rely on depth or simple RGB-D fusion and fail where candidate waypoints share similar spatial structure. Traditional topological maps and uneven data sampling also degrade navigation decisions.
motivation: Accurate waypoint prediction and good decision-making are the two bottlenecks of continuous-environment VLN. The paper argues that aligned visual-textual cues improve waypoint prediction, and that combining memory of panoramic environment data with detailed current observations improves planning.
key_idea: Combine an observation-driven waypoint predictor, which fuses spatial data with aligned vision-language cues, with a memory-observation planner that uses panoramic memory together with the current detailed observation.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that language-aligned visual cues disambiguate waypoints with similar geometry, and that memory plus current observation gives better decisions than topological maps alone.
method: Observation-driven waypoint predictor: uses depth spatial data and integrates aligned visual and textual cues to predict waypoints more accurately.
Memory-observation planning: uses memory panoramic environment data and detailed current observation information for navigation decisions.
Discrete adaptation: the framework is also adapted to the discrete R2R setting.

numbers.evidence: Abstract: achieving a 60.25% Success Rate (SR) and a 50.89% Path Length Score (SPL) on the R2R-CE dataset's unseen validation splits
Abstract: achieving a 74% SR and a 64% SPL on the unseen validation split

numbers_note: abstract only; NE, OSR and other metrics are not available
results: MossVLN reports 60.25 SR and 50.89 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen. Adapted to discrete R2R, it reports 74 SR and 64 SPL on val-unseen. Baselines are not named in the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details, ablations and baselines are unknown.
Dependence on a waypoint predictor is implied by the design.
